chapter.li: LEChapter59 Verse1 Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi, after Moroni had received and had read Helaman’s epistle, he was exceedingly rejoiced because of the welfare, yea, the exceeding success which Helaman had had in obtaining those lands which were lost. VerseEnd Verse2 Yea, and he did make it known unto all his people in all the land round about in that part where he was, that they might rejoice also. VerseEnd

Verse3 And it came to pass that he immediately sent an epistle to Parhoron, desiring that he should cause men to be gathered together to strengthen Helaman, or the armies of Helaman, insomuch that he might with ease maintain that part of the land which he had been so miraculously prospered in retaining. VerseEnd Verse4 And it came to pass when Moroni had sent this epistle to the land of Zarahemla, he began again to lay a plan that he might obtain the remainder of those possessions and cities which the Lamanites had taken from them. VerseEnd

Verse5 And it came to pass that while Moroni was thus making preparations to go against the Lamanites to battle, behold, the people of Nephihah who were gathered together from the city of Moroni, and the city of Lehi, and the city of Morionton, were attacked by the Lamanites. VerseEnd Verse6 Yea, even those who had been compelled to flee from the land of Manti and from the land round about had come over and joined the Lamanites in this part of the land. VerseEnd Verse7 And thus being exceeding numerous, yea, and receiving strength from day to day by the command of Ammoron, they came forth against the people of Nephihah and they did begin to slay them with an exceeding great slaughter. VerseEnd Verse8 And their armies were so numerous that the remainder of the people of Nephihah were obliged to flee before them; and they came even and joined the army of Moroni. VerseEnd Verse9 And now, as Moroni had supposed that there should be men sent to the city of Nephihah, to the assistance of the people to maintain that city, and knowing that it was easier to keep the city from falling into the hands of the Lamanites than to retake it from them, he supposed that they would easily maintain that city; VerseEnd Verse10 therefore he retained all his force to maintain those places which he had recovered. VerseEnd

Verse11 And now when Moroni saw that the city of Nephihah was lost, he was exceeding sorrowful and began to doubt, because of the wickedness of the people, whether they should not fall into the hands of their brethren. VerseEnd Verse12 Now this was the case with all his chief captains. They doubted and marveled also because of the wickedness of the people, and this because of the success of the Lamanites over them. VerseEnd Verse13 And it came to pass that Moroni was angry with the government because of their indifference concerning the freedom of their country. VerseEnd

LEChapter60 Verse1 And it came to pass that he wrote again to the governor of the land, who was Parhoron, and these are the words which he wrote, saying, Behold, I direct mine epistle to Parhoron in the city of Zarahemla, who is the chief judge and the governor over the land, and also to all those who have been chosen by this people to govern and manage the affairs of this war; VerseEnd Verse2 for behold, I have somewhat to say unto them by the way of condemnation. For behold, 2PP ye yourselves know that 2PP ye have been appointed to gather together men and arm them with swords, and with cimeters, and all manner of weapons of war of every kind, and send forth against the Lamanites in whatsoever parts they should come into our land. VerseEnd Verse3 And now behold, I say unto 2PP you that myself, and also my men, and also Helaman and his men, have suffered exceeding great sufferings — yea, even hunger, thirst, and fatigue, and all manner of afflictions of every kind. VerseEnd Verse4 But behold, were this all we had suffered, we would not murmur nor complain; VerseEnd Verse5 but behold, great has been the slaughter among our people, yea, thousands have fallen by the sword, while it might have otherwise been if 2PP ye had rendered unto our armies sufficient strength and succor for them. Yea, great has been 2PP your neglect towards us. VerseEnd

Verse6 And now behold, we desire to know the cause of this exceeding great neglect; yea, we desire to know the cause of 2PP your thoughtless state. VerseEnd Verse7 Can 2PP you think to sit upon 2PP your thrones in a state of thoughtless stupor while 2PP your enemies are spreading the work of death around 2PP you? Yea, while they are murdering thousands of 2PP your brethren? VerseEnd Verse8 Yea, even they who have looked up to 2PP you for protection, yea, have placed 2PP you in a situation that 2PP ye might have succored them. Yea, 2PP ye might have sent armies unto them to have strengthened them and have saved thousands of them from falling by the sword. VerseEnd Verse9 But behold, this is not all. 2PP Ye have withheld 2PP your provisions from them, insomuch that many have fought and bled out their lives because of their great desires which they had for the welfare of this people; yea, and this they have done when they were about to perish with hunger because of 2PP your exceeding great neglect towards them. VerseEnd Verse10 And now, my beloved brethren — for 2PP ye had ought to be beloved, yea, and 2PP ye had ought to have stirred yourselves more diligently for the welfare and the freedom of this people. But behold, 2PP ye have neglected them, insomuch that the blood of thousands shall come upon 2PP your heads for vengeance; yea, for known unto God were all their cries and all their sufferings. VerseEnd Verse11 Behold, could 2PP ye suppose that 2PP ye could sit upon 2PP your thrones and because of the exceeding goodness of God 2PP ye could do nothing and he would deliver 2PP you? Behold, if 2PP ye have supposed this, 2PP ye have supposed in vain. VerseEnd Verse12 Do 2PP ye suppose that because so many of 2PP your brethren have been killed, it is because of their wickedness? I say unto 2PP you, if 2PP ye have supposed this, 2PP ye have supposed in vain. For I say unto 2PP you, there are many who have fallen by the sword, and behold, it is to 2PP your condemnation. VerseEnd Verse13 For the Lord suffereth the righteous to be slain that his justice and judgment may come upon the wicked; therefore 2PP ye need not suppose that the righteous are lost because they are slain, but behold, they do enter into the rest of the Lord their God. VerseEnd

Verse14 And now behold, I say unto 2PP you, I fear exceedingly that the judgments of God will come upon this people because of their exceeding slothfulness, yea, even the slothfulness of our government and their exceeding great neglect towards their brethren, yea, towards those who have been slain. VerseEnd Verse15 For were it not for the wickedness which first commenced at our head, we could have withstood our enemies, that they could have gained no power over us. VerseEnd Verse16 Yea, had it not been for the war which broke out among ourselves, yea, were it not for those Kingmen who caused so much bloodshed among ourselves, yea, at the time we were contending among ourselves — if we had united our strength as we hitherto have done, yea, had it not been for the desire of power and authority which those Kingmen had over us, had they been true to the cause of our freedom and united with us, and gone forth against our enemies instead of taking up their swords against us, which was the cause of so much bloodshed among ourselves — yea, if we had gone forth against them in the strength of the Lord, we should have dispersed our enemies, for it would have been done according to the fulfilling of his word. VerseEnd Verse17 But behold, now the Lamanites are coming upon us and they are murdering our people with the sword, yea, our women and our children, taking possession of our lands, and also carrying them away captive, causing them that they should suffer all manner of afflictions, and this because of the great wickedness of those who are seeking for power and authority, yea, even those Kingmen. VerseEnd

Verse18 But why should I say much concerning this matter? For we know not but what 2PP ye yourselves are seeking for authority; we know not but what 2PP ye are also traitors to 2PP your country. VerseEnd Verse19 Or is it that 2PP ye have neglected us because 2PP ye are in the heart of our country and 2PP ye are surrounded by security, that 2PP ye do not cause food to be sent unto us and also men to strengthen our armies? VerseEnd Verse20 Have 2PP ye forgat the commandments of the Lord 2PP your God? Yea, have 2PP ye forgat the captivity of our fathers? Have 2PP ye forgat the many times we have been delivered out of the hands of our enemies? VerseEnd Verse21 Or do 2PP ye suppose that the Lord will still deliver us while we sit upon our thrones and do not make use of the means which the Lord has provided for us? VerseEnd Verse22 Yea, will 2PP ye sit in idleness while 2PP ye are surrounded with thousands of those, yea, and tens of thousands, who do also sit in idleness, while there are thousands round about in the borders of the land who are falling by the sword? Yea, wounded and bleeding? VerseEnd Verse23 Do 2PP ye suppose that God will look upon 2PP you as guiltless while 2PP ye sit still and behold these things? Behold, I say unto 2PP you, nay.

Now I would that 2PP ye should remember that God has said that the inward vessel shall be cleansed first, and then shall the outer vessel be cleansed also. VerseEnd Verse24 And now except 2PP ye do repent of that which 2PP ye have done, and begin to be up and doing, and send forth food and men unto us, and also unto Helaman, that he may support those parts of our country which he hath retained, and that we may also recover the remainder of our possessions in these parts, behold, it will be expedient that we contend no more with the Lamanites until we have first cleansed our inward vessel, yea, even the great head of our government. VerseEnd Verse25 And except 2PP ye grant mine epistle, and come out and shew unto me a true spirit of freedom, and strive to strengthen and fortify our armies, and grant unto them food for their support, behold, I will leave a part of my Freemen to maintain this part of our land, and I will leave the strength and the blessings of God upon them, that none other power can operate against them — VerseEnd Verse26 and this because of their exceeding faith and their patience in their tribulations — VerseEnd Verse27 and I will come unto 2PP you; and if there be any among 2PP you that has a desire for freedom, yea, if there be even a spark of freedom remaining, behold, I will stir up insurrections among 2PP you, even until those who have desires to usurp power and authority shall become extinct. VerseEnd Verse28 Yea, behold, I do not fear 2PP your power nor 2PP your authority, but it is my God whom I fear; and it is according to his commandments that I do take my sword to defend the cause of my country, and it is because of 2PP your iniquity that we have suffered so much loss. VerseEnd

Verse29 Behold, it is time, yea, the time is now at hand that except 2PP ye do bestir yourselves in the defense of 2PP your country and 2PP your little ones, the sword of justice doth hang over 2PP you, yea, and it shall fall upon 2PP you and visit 2PP you, even to 2PP your utter destruction. VerseEnd Verse30 Behold, I wait for assistance from 2PP you; and except 2PP ye do administer unto our relief, behold, I come unto 2PP you, even into the land of Zarahemla, and smite 2PP you with the sword, insomuch that 2PP ye can have no more power to impede the progress of this people in the cause of our freedom. VerseEnd Verse31 For behold, the Lord will not suffer that 2PP ye shall live and wax strong in 2PP your iniquities to destroy his righteous people. VerseEnd Verse32 Behold, can 2PP you suppose that the Lord will spare 2PP you and come out in judgment against the Lamanites when it is the tradition of their fathers that has caused their hatred — yea, and it has been redoubled by those who have dissented from us — while 2PP your iniquity is for the cause of 2PP your love of glory and the vain things of the world? VerseEnd Verse33 2PP Ye know that 2PP ye do transgress the laws of God, and 2PP ye do know that 2PP ye do trample them under 2PP your feet. Behold, the Lord saith unto me, If those whom 2PP ye have appointed 2PP your governors do not repent of their sins and iniquities, 2PP ye shall go up to battle against them. VerseEnd

Verse34 And now behold, I, Moroni, am constrained according to the covenant which I have made to keep the commandments of my God, therefore I would that 2PP ye should adhere to the word of God and send speedily unto me of 2PP your provisions and of 2PP your men, and also to Helaman. VerseEnd Verse35 And behold, if 2PP ye will not do this, I come unto 2PP you speedily. For behold, God will not suffer that we should perish with hunger, therefore he will give unto us of 2PP your food, even if it must be by the sword. Now see that 2PP ye fulfill the word of God. VerseEnd Verse36 Behold, I am Moroni, 2PP your chief captain. I seek not for power, but to pull it down. I seek not for honor of the world, but for the glory of my God and the freedom and welfare of my country. And thus I close mine epistle. VerseEnd
